dek: Claude's maker could top SpaceX's record IPO despite a historic net loss.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Anthropic, maker of the *Claude* AI model, filed to go public, with a possible *$2 trillion* valuation.

slides.label: The numbers
slides.text: Revenue grew *1,050%* to $4.6 billion in 2025, but net losses hit a staggering *$42 billion*.

slides.label: Inside the loss
slides.text: About *$34 billion* of that came from an accounting charge; the real operating loss was *$8 billion*.

slides.label: Where it's spent
slides.text: Anthropic spent *$7.3 billion* on compute in 2025 (up from $400 million in 2023), 58% of its costs.

slides.label: The risk warning
slides.text: Its own filing warns advanced AI could pose *"catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."*

slides.label: Not alone
slides.text: OpenAI's *Sam Altman* has urged AI companies to slow down over similar safety concerns.

slides.label: What's next
slides.text: Anthropic would be the *first frontier AI lab* to go public, facing intense investor scrutiny.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: For underrepresented founders, it's a reminder: AI money moves fast, but so do the risks and the hype.

cta_line: The AI money race just got *bigger*.
question: Hype or red flag? One word.

caption_instagram:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI model, just filed for an IPO that could value it at $2 trillion, enough to beat SpaceX as the biggest IPO ever. According to The Motley Fool, the filing also revealed a staggering $42 billion net loss for 2025, even as revenue jumped 1,050% to $4.6 billion.

Most of that loss came from an accounting charge, but the real operating loss still sits around $8 billion, driven by the $7.3 billion Anthropic spent on compute power. The filing even admits advanced AI could pose "existential risks to humanity," a warning OpenAI's Sam Altman has echoed by telling the industry to slow down.

This would be the first frontier AI lab to test public markets, and every founder building in AI (especially those without deep pockets) should be watching how investors react.

Hype or red flag? One word.
